about: Hand-maintained source of docs/OWNER_MANUAL_LANES.md. Edit this file, then run: uv run python scripts/build_owner_manual.py. Card text is plain words; .. marks bold. Built-versus-manual, county access, adapters and dormant scrapers are computed by the generator, not typed here.
what_changed: The manual is now generated (scripts/build_owner_manual.py) from structured data: the county matrix, the register-platform cluster docs, every new_sources JSON, the gap matrix, the live run status, the registered deed adapters and this register. 'python scripts/build_owner_manual.py --check' says when it is stale.

County access and the 'built' list are computed: a county whose deed search has a registered reader shows the reader and its on/off switch; a plain 'I agree', disclosure popup or credential-free guest button is always allowed, never a wall.
Every walled record in the source-hunt files appears in a generated table, with the card that covers it or 'no card yet'.

kind_def.A: A: a person passes it in a normal browser. A CAPTCHA (click pictures or tick 'I'm not a robot'), a Cloudflare or similar bot check ('Just a moment...', 'Verify you are human', 'Access Denied'), or a real login (an account with a user name and password, even a free one you make yourself).
kind_def.B: B: paid or attorney-only. A per-page fee, a subscription, a license (MLS), or an agency-only sign-in.
kind_def.C: C: allowed (not a wall). Terms of use, a robots.txt line, or a plain click with no credentials: 'I agree', a disclaimer, a disclosure popup, or a 'Sign in as a Guest' button. These are built or buildable and listed in appendix C.

decisions: A plain 'I agree', disclaimer, disclosure popup or 'Sign in as a Guest' button that asks for no credentials is not a wall (Kania, Zacchaeus, Aldridge Pite, and the ten Cott guest-button deed counties: Alamance, Edgecombe, Halifax, Lenoir, Onslow, Pitt, Rowan, Rutherford, Scotland, Wilson).

Terms-only restrictions; the SC Judicial Branch Public Index terms (Rule 610 and the administrative order); SC Code 30-2-50 for our SC mailings; AI cold calls. The Public Index automation was then stopped by a technical bot check (HTTP 406 at the site's edge, plus a script challenge), so those lists stay a hand-save card; Charleston's own copy of the Index is open and buildable.

The LiensNC login lives in the LiensNC scripts by the owner's choice, so pulls stay repeatable. The full run never re-scraped LiensNC (national.liensnc is disabled); the roughly 45,000 rows on the board came from the two manual scripts (scripts/scrape_liensnc.py, then scripts/ingest_all.py). A repeatable incremental LiensNC refresh through the Mac hand-off is being built.

manual_intro: Only four things keep a source manual: a CAPTCHA, a Cloudflare or other bot check, a real login (an account with a password), or a payment or attorney-only subscription. Each card below is one such source, sorted inside its group by value for your time: the start page, the clicks (including how a person gets past the check in a normal browser), what to pull, how to save it and where to put it, how it gets loaded, time and how often, what we gain, and who else could do it.
appendix_c_intro: No technical barrier: terms of use, robots.txt, or a plain click with no credentials. The attorney has cleared terms-only limits, and robots.txt is not a wall by the owner's rule. If a CAPTCHA, a real login or a bot check ever appears on one of these, it moves to type A and the reader stops.

cards.place: North Carolina, every county (start with the 11 core counties)
cards.name: NC court foreclosure cases (special proceedings) on the NC eCourts portal
cards.wall: Picture CAPTCHA ("Let's confirm you are human") in front of every search. Scripts get an HTTP 405 'Human Verification' page.
cards.what: Every power-of-sale foreclosure in NC is a court 'special proceeding' (case numbers like 26SP000500-100). The law-firm sale calendars and newspaper notices we already read cover many of them, but not all, and not the case status (hearing held, sale held, upset bid filed). Without this we miss foreclosures no law firm posts, and we cannot tell which sales are still open.
steps: Open Chrome (a normal window) and go to https://portal-nc.tylertech.cloud/Portal/. Use that exact address; the bare site name shows an error page. Do not sign in. The public search needs no account.
Click Smart Search.
In the search box type 26SP* (all 2026 special proceedings). Use 25SP* for last year if you are backfilling.

Click Advanced Filtering Options. Set Location to the county (for example 'Buncombe County'). Set the File Date range: first time, the last 6 months; after that, from your last pull to today. (Labels can differ slightly; pick the closest match.)

Click Submit. A box that says "Let's confirm you are human" with a grid of pictures may appear. Click the pictures it asks for, then press Confirm. It can ask two or three times in a row; that is normal. Do not use any add-on or service that solves it for you.
At the bottom of the results, set items per page to the largest number offered (200). If the list looks short (about 23 rows), the site is sampling: narrow the dates and search again.
Press Cmd + S. Set Format to Web Page, HTML Only (not Complete, not PDF).
Name the file <county>_nc_sp_<date>.html, for example buncombe_nc_sp_2026-10-07.html (two-word counties: new_hanover_nc_sp_2026-10-07.html). Save it into the Desktop folder Court Pages (drop here).
Repeat for the next county. The CAPTCHA usually does not come back for a few minutes.
When all counties are saved, double-click Ingest Saved Court Pages on the Desktop. A notice tells you how many NC court records it found.

Optional, for earlier warning: the portal's hearing search (same CAPTCHA) lists power-of-sale hearings before the notice of sale. Search hearings by county and date range with case type Special Proceedings and save the results the same way (name <county>_nc_hearings_<date>.html).
cards.pull: Only rows whose case type reads Foreclosure (Special Proceeding). Keep the columns the grid shows: case number, case style (the parties, which names the owner), file date, location, status. One results page per county per pull. Weekly: the 11 core counties (Buncombe, Henderson, Cleveland, Gaston, Rutherford, Polk, Transylvania, McDowell, Lincoln, Mitchell, Burke). Monthly: the next 14 by lead count (Mecklenburg, Wake, Forsyth, Guilford, Catawba, New Hanover, Brunswick, Durham, Pitt, Orange, Johnston, Union, Onslow, Harnett). Check: the number after the dash in each case number is the county code (Buncombe ends in -100).
cards.save: Web Page, HTML Only. Filename must contain _nc_ (the loader reads the county from the text before it). Folder: ~/Desktop/Court Pages (drop here)/. Then run the Desktop app Ingest Saved Court Pages.
cards.lane: Existing. The app runs the saved-page reader for NC court pages, which is tested on this exact results grid (verified 2026-08-13), turns each row into a lead, and tries to match the owner name to a parcel. The app refuses to run while the weekly engine run is writing, and never makes duplicates. For the engineer: scripts/ingest_saved.sh, scripts/parse_nc_ecourts_export.py, scripts/ingest_fresh_court_leads.py.
cards.time: About 2 to 3 minutes per county once past the CAPTCHA: 30 minutes for the 11 core counties, 35 more for the monthly 14.
cards.gain: New NC foreclosure cases the law firms do not post, with the owner's name and case number; earlier warning on cases still in the hearing stage. Our estimate (not measured): 15 to 40 new cases a week across the 11 core counties. Name-to-parcel matching runs about 30% automatically, so expect roughly a third to land on a property without your help.
cards.others: The Clerk of Superior Court's public terminal in each courthouse (free, in person). A title abstractor or a title company's foreclosure report (an O&E report runs about $85 to $95 per property, per our notes). The attorney's own research subscription (Westlaw or Lexis docket search, if his plan includes NC dockets; price not on file).

cards.place: North Carolina, every county (start with the 11 core counties)
cards.name: NC estate files (probate) on the NC eCourts portal
cards.wall: The same picture CAPTCHA as above.
cards.what: Every NC estate is opened with the Clerk of Superior Court and indexed on eCourts (case numbers like 26E000123-100). Newspaper notices to creditors reach us for many estates, but only after the executor publishes, and only the ones that publish where we read. The estate index shows the decedent and the date the estate opened, weeks earlier.
steps: Open Chrome (a normal window) and go to https://portal-nc.tylertech.cloud/Portal/. Use that exact address; the bare site name shows an error page. Do not sign in. The public search needs no account.
Click Smart Search.
In the search box type 26E* (all 2026 estate files).

Click Advanced Filtering Options. Set Location to the county and the File Date range (first time: last 6 months; after that: since your last pull). If a Case Category or Case Type filter is offered, pick Estate.

Click Submit. A box that says "Let's confirm you are human" with a grid of pictures may appear. Click the pictures it asks for, then press Confirm. It can ask two or three times in a row; that is normal. Do not use any add-on or service that solves it for you.
At the bottom of the results, set items per page to the largest number offered (200). If the list looks short (about 23 rows), the site is sampling: narrow the dates and search again.
Press Cmd + S. Set Format to Web Page, HTML Only (not Complete, not PDF).
Name the file <county>_nc_estates_<date>.html, for example henderson_nc_estates_2026-10-07.html. Save it into Court Pages (drop here) on the Desktop.
Repeat per county, then double-click Ingest Saved Court Pages.
cards.pull: All estate rows (decedent estates). Skip guardianship, incompetency, minor and other rows that describe a living person's health or capacity; they are not property leads and should not be saved. Columns: case number, case name (the decedent), file date, location, status. Same county plan as the foreclosure search: core 11 weekly, next 14 monthly.
cards.save: Web Page, HTML Only, filename with _nc_, into Court Pages (drop here), then the Desktop app.
cards.lane: Existing (same app and reader as the foreclosure search). The reader recognizes estate captions ('Estate of ...', 'In re ...') and scores these rows as estate leads. First time you do this, ask Claude to check that the decedent names came through correctly.
cards.time: About 2 minutes per county: 25 minutes for the core 11.
cards.gain: The decedent's name and the estate's opening date, weeks before any newspaper notice. Your sheet shows estate and probate signals at zero or under 1% in most NC counties. Our estimate (not measured): 50 to 100 new estates a week across the core 11; many will not own land.
cards.others: The Clerk's Estates Division (public terminal or a phone call, free). The attorney's research subscription if it covers NC estate dockets (price not on file). Paid court-data vendors (UniCourt, Trellis; price not on file).

cards.place: North Carolina, one lead at a time
cards.name: Check one NC lead's court case (status, parties, heirs) with the human-assisted checker
cards.wall: The same picture CAPTCHA, plus the NC Secretary of State's bot check when the owner is a company.
cards.what: For a HOT lead (lis pendens, foreclosure, divorce or estate), the one fact that decides whether to call is on the case page: is the case still open, who are the parties, are there heirs we do not know about. We have a tool that sets this up and reads the saved page.
steps: Tell Claude: "verify lead <parcel number> in <county>" (or give the case number). The tool prints which search to run and opens the eCourts page in your browser. If the owner is a company, a second tab opens on the NC Secretary of State business search.
On eCourts: pass the picture CAPTCHA yourself, search the case number (best) or the name it printed, and click into the matching case so the full case page shows (parties, events, hearings).
Press Cmd + S, Web Page, HTML Only, and save it as <parcel>_case.html in your Downloads folder.
If the company tab opened: search the company name, open its profile page, save it the same way as <parcel>_sos.html.

Tell Claude the file names. The tool reads them and reports confirmed, refuted or unconfirmed. For an estate, any new name on the page is checked against the free NC voter list to see if that person is alive and where they vote.
cards.pull: One case page per lead: the parties list, the events list (hearing, order of sale, upset bid, dismissal) and the status line. Do HOT leads only, 5 per sitting.
cards.save: HTML Only, in ~/Downloads, filename with the parcel number. Do not put these in the court drop folder (they are single cases, not lists).
cards.lane: Existing, run by Claude in the terminal: the tool queues the check, opens the page, and parses what you saved into a verdict. It does not write back to the dashboard yet; the verdict is a report. For the engineer: scripts/verify_lead_human_assisted.py, src/foreclosure_scraper/verification_human_lane.py.
cards.gain: A checked yes or no on the lead's case, and the heirs list on estate leads. This adds no new cells to your sheet; it makes the leads you call right.
cards.others: The attorney (his eCourts access is the same public search; his staff can run it). A title abstractor for heirs on a specific property.

cards.place: North Carolina, newspaper legal notices (statewide site)
cards.name: Full text of NC estate and foreclosure notices on ncnotices.com
cards.wall: Each notice's full text sits behind an 'I Agree, View Notice' click (allowed) and, on the notices our reader checked, a Google checkbox CAPTCHA ('I'm not a robot'), which is what keeps it manual.
cards.what: We already read the notice list (name, county, date). The full text holds the executor's name and mailing address, the attorney, and sometimes the date of death. That is the best free contact path for an estate.
steps: Open https://www.ncnotices.com/ in Chrome.
Search the decedent's name from the lead (or browse 'Notice to Creditors' for the county).
Click the notice. Tick the box I'm not a robot, pass any picture check, and click I Agree, View Notice.
Copy the executor (personal representative) name and mailing address, the attorney's name, and the date of death if shown.
Paste them into the lead's notes in your CRM. If you prefer, save the notice page (Cmd + S, HTML Only) into ~/Downloads as <parcel>_notice.html, but no reader picks these up yet.
cards.pull: For estate leads you will actually mail or call: executor name, executor mailing address, attorney, date of death. 10 per sitting.
cards.save: Type into the CRM. Saved pages are not loaded by anything yet.
cards.lane: None. A small reader would be needed: the notice-body reader we already have for the ungated notices could read a saved page. About an hour for the engineer.
cards.gain: A named, mailable executor for the estate (the person who can sign). Your sheet shows 'heir naming publication' at zero in every NC county.
cards.others: The executor's attorney is named in the notice; the attorney's office is a legitimate contact route.

cards.place: North Carolina, Secretary of State
cards.name: NC Secretary of State: federal tax lien and UCC lien searches
cards.wall: Cloudflare check ('Just a moment...' or a 'Verify you are human' box) that our stealth browser could not pass. The federal tax lien page also says scripted searches are not permitted and bulk access is a paid data subscription (price not on file).
cards.what: IRS liens and UCC filings against companies (LLCs, builders) that own our leads. A narrow signal: it only covers company owners.
steps: Open the page in Chrome. If the Cloudflare box shows, tick it.
Type the company name exactly as the county shows the owner (for example 'ABC HOLDINGS LLC'). Search.
Open each hit and note: filing date, lien amount if shown, the IRS office, and whether it is released.
For UCC filings use https://www.sosnc.gov/online_services/search/by_title/_uniform_commercial_code the same way.
cards.pull: Company-owned HOT leads only. Filing date, amount, status (open or released). 10 names per sitting.
cards.save: Type into the CRM. No reader exists.
cards.lane: None. A two-column file (owner name, lien note) could be loaded later if this proves useful.
cards.gain: Proof of tax trouble for company owners. Your sheet's 'liens' column is zero in every NC county, but this source fills only the company-owned slice.
cards.others: The NC SoS paid data subscription for bulk (price not on file). The attorney's lien search vendor.

cards.place: South Carolina: Aiken, Bamberg, Barnwell, Charleston, Cherokee, Chester, Colleton, Dorchester, Florence, Georgetown, Kershaw, Lancaster, Marlboro, Oconee, Orangeburg, Sumter, York
cards.name: SC probate court estate index on southcarolinaprobate.net
cards.wall: The site refuses scripts with a 403 'Forbidden' page from its load balancer (checked 2026-10-07, also with a normal browser identity). A person in a normal browser should get the search page. If you also get 403 in your own browser, the site is down; call the probate court.
cards.what: 17 SC probate courts post their estate index here. Each estate row shows the decedent, the filing date, the case status, the creditor-claim deadline and, in a sub-table, the personal representative's full name and mailing address. Our reader for this site works only when the site answers it, and today it does not.
steps: Open https://www.southcarolinaprobate.net/search/ in Chrome. (Charleston also has /charlestonprobatesearch/.)
Pick the county in the County drop-down. Wait for the page to refresh.
Type a last name in the name box and press Search. The site searches by name only, not by date. Use the surnames of your SC obituary, estate and tax-delinquent leads in that county.
Click the plus sign on each matching case to open the parties list (the personal representative's name and address) and the docket list.
Press Cmd + S, Web Page, HTML Only. Name: <county>_sc_probate_<surname>_<date>.html.
cards.pull: Estate cases only (skip marriage records). Case number, decedent, filing date, status, creditor-claim date, personal representative name and mailing address. 15 surnames per sitting, biggest counties first (Charleston, Sumter, Oconee, Cherokee, Florence, Colleton).
cards.save: HTML Only into ~/Downloads (not the court drop folder, which would move the files without reading them).
cards.lane: None for saved pages yet. The live reader already parses this exact page (it is how the 373 Charleston rows on the board were built), so pointing it at saved files is a small job, about an hour. Until then, ask Claude to load them by hand. For the engineer: src/foreclosure_scraper/scrapers/counties_sc/sc_probate_net.py.
cards.time: About 1 minute per surname search plus 1 minute per case opened.
cards.gain: SC estates with a named personal representative and a mailing address, which is the person who can sell. Your sheet shows SC probate and estate signals at zero or under 1% in about 35 to 45 of 46 SC counties.
cards.others: The probate court clerk by phone (free). The attorney's probate subscription where a county sells document access (Greenville). An SC abstractor.

cards.place: South Carolina, Secretary of State
cards.name: SC Secretary of State business entity search (company owners)
cards.wall: Google checkbox CAPTCHA ('I'm not a robot') on every search (re-checked 2026-10-04).
cards.what: When an SC lead is owned by an LLC or corporation, the entity record shows whether it is in good standing or dissolved, the registered agent's name and address, and sometimes the principal office. NC company owners we already look up for free; SC we cannot.
steps: Open the page in Chrome.
Type the company name as the county shows it. Tick I'm not a robot and pass any picture check. Press Search.
Open the matching entity. Note: status (Good Standing, Forfeited, Dissolved), date of status, registered agent name and address.
Type these into the lead's notes in the CRM.
cards.pull: SC HOT and WARM leads whose owner name contains LLC, INC, CORP, TRUST or LP. Status, status date, registered agent name and address. 10 per sitting.
cards.save: Type into the CRM. No reader exists (an older instruction to save 'sc_sos_<entity>.html' files led nowhere: nothing reads them).
cards.lane: None. A small reader for a saved entity page, or a simple CSV (owner name, status, agent, agent address), would be needed.
cards.gain: A contact route (the registered agent) and a distress flag (forfeited or dissolved company still holding land). Your sheet's 'SoS dissolution' column is zero in all 46 SC counties.
cards.others: The SC UCC search (ucconline.sc.gov) for liens against company owners: the 2026-10-07 source hunt found it open; an older note said $5 a search. The attorney's corporate search vendor.
covers: SC Secretary of State business filings search

cards.place: South Carolina, newspaper legal notices
cards.name: Full text of SC notices to creditors and foreclosure notices (scpublicnotices.com, publicnoticesc.com)
cards.wall: scpublicnotices.com: the notice page ('Details') shows a Cloudflare 'Verify you are human' box and a Google CAPTCHA. publicnoticesc.com: Cloudflare check on every page.

steps: Open https://www.scpublicnotices.com/ in Chrome.
Search the decedent's or owner's last name, or filter by county and category (Notice to Creditors, Foreclosure).
Click the notice. Pass the 'Verify you are human' box and the picture check if shown.
Copy the personal representative's name and address (estates) or sale date, address and plaintiff (foreclosures) into the CRM.

cards.pull: Top SC estate and foreclosure leads only: representative name, mailing address, attorney; or sale date and address. 10 per sitting.
cards.save: Type into the CRM. Nothing reads saved notice pages yet.
cards.lane: None. Same small reader job as the NC notice bodies.
cards.gain: Named contacts on SC estates. Your sheet's 'heir naming publication' column is zero in 45 of 46 SC counties.
cards.others: The attorney named in the notice.

cards.place: South Carolina, county property cards on qPublic: Allendale, Bamberg, Barnwell, Cherokee, Chester, Clarendon, Colleton, Darlington, Edgefield, Fairfield, Florence, Georgetown, Hampton, Jasper, Kershaw, Lancaster, Laurens, Lee, Marlboro, Newberry, Oconee, Orangeburg, Pickens, Spartanburg, Union, York
cards.name: SC assessor property cards (heated square feet, beds, baths, sales) on qPublic
cards.wall: Cloudflare 'Verify you are human' check on searches (a terms click also shows; that part is allowed).
cards.what: Free SC map layers leave heated square feet and sale price blank. The county property card on qPublic has them as plain text. Without them our value estimates for SC lean on guesses.
steps: Open the qPublic link for the county (replace Cherokee in the address with the county name, for example App=PickensCountySC).
Click through the terms box. If a Cloudflare 'Verify you are human' box shows, tick it.
Search by Parcel ID (the lead's TMS number) or by owner name.
On the card, find Heated Sq Ft (or Living Area), Bedrooms, Full Baths, Year Built, Acres, and the Sales table (date, price, deed book and page).
Type these into the CRM, or into a simple sheet with columns: parcel_id, heated_sqft, beds, baths, year_built, last_sale_date, last_sale_price.
cards.pull: SC HOT leads with no square footage on the dashboard. The 7 fields above. 10 parcels per sitting.
cards.save: A CSV with the columns above, saved as sc_cards_<date>.csv in ~/Downloads, then ask Claude to load it. Saved card pages are not read by anything.
cards.lane: None for a hand-made CSV. A small loader (parcel_id plus the 7 fields) is about an hour of work. Note for the engineer: the code that renders these cards automatically has a setting that ticks the Cloudflare box unless FORECLOSURE_NO_CF_SOLVE=1 is set, and no run script sets it. That should be checked against the owner's rule.
cards.gain: Real square footage and sale history, which make the value estimate and the offer price trustworthy. Your sheet shows square feet zero in 26 SC counties and beds and baths zero in 31.
cards.others: The county assessor's office (call with the TMS number). Paid property data: ATTOM (entry about $95 to $500 a month; bulk backfill $1,500 to $5,000 one time), Realie ($50 to $350 a month), PropStream Pro ($199 a month). Prices from our 2026-07 notes; confirm before buying.

cards.place: South Carolina, 45 county courts on publicindex.sccourts.org (Charleston has its own open copy)
cards.name: SC Judicial Public Index case lists (foreclosure, partition, quiet title, lis pendens, judgments)
cards.wall: A bot check, not the terms: the terms (Rule 610 and the administrative order) are cleared by the attorney, but on 2026-10-07 the site's edge refused an ordinary request with HTTP 406 on every path, and earlier checks found an F5 'Client Challenge' script on the search page. A person's desktop browser passes both without seeing anything. So the automatic lanes were not built, and these lists are hand-saved (docs/new_sources_2026-10-07_sc_public_index.md).
cards.what: SC foreclosure, partition, quiet-title, lis pendens and judgment case lists for 45 counties. SC foreclosure is judicial, so this is where an SC foreclosure starts. Your sheet shows SC foreclosure-sale signals at zero in 39 of 46 counties.
steps: Open https://publicindex.sccourts.org/<County>/PublicIndex/ in Chrome (for example Spartanburg). Click Accept on the disclaimer.
Leave Last Name blank. Set Date Type to Case Filed, the begin date to your last pull (first time: 6 months back), the end date to today.

Run each lane and save each results page: Foreclosure (Circuit Court, Common Pleas, sub-type Foreclosure 420); Partition (sub-type Partition 440); Quiet title (the quiet-title sub-type in the Common Pleas list); Lis Pendens (Index Search radio, Lis Pendens); Judgments (Index Search radio, Judgments). Skip Possession/eviction (it names the tenant, not the owner).
If it says 'maximum records exceeded', shorten the date range to about 2 months.

Press Cmd + S, HTML Only, name <county>_sc_<lane>_<date>.html (for example spartanburg_sc_foreclosure_2026-10-07.html), save into Court Pages (drop here), then run the Desktop app Ingest Saved Court Pages.
cards.pull: Foreclosure and partition first, then quiet title, lis pendens and judgments. Case number, caption, filed date, status. Monthly: the 7 core SC counties (Spartanburg, Anderson, Pickens, Oconee, Cherokee, Union, Laurens), then Greenville, Horry, York, Lexington, Richland, Berkeley, Sumter as time allows. For Master in Equity sale rosters (York, Aiken, Lexington, Richland and others), open Court Rosters on the same site and save the month's roster page.
cards.save: HTML Only into Court Pages (drop here), then Ingest Saved Court Pages.
cards.lane: Existing: the app runs the SC Public Index reader automatically on any saved Public Index page. The list page has no judgment dollar column (an older bug that read the case-number year as a '$2026' judgment was fixed on 2026-09-29). Charleston's own copy (jcmsweb.charlestoncounty.org/PublicIndex/) answered normally and is buildable. For the engineer: scripts/ingest_publicindex_files.py; src/foreclosure_scraper/ingest_sc_publicindex_export.py.
cards.time: About 3 minutes per county per lane: about 40 minutes a month for foreclosure and partition in the 7 core counties.
cards.gain: SC foreclosure and partition filings, the first public sign of an SC foreclosure, plus quiet-title and judgment filings.
cards.others: The Clerk of Court (records request). Paid court data (UniCourt, Trellis; prices not on file).

cards.place: Nationwide (federal bankruptcy courts for Western, Middle and Eastern NC and for SC)
cards.name: PACER bankruptcy petitions: fix the bankruptcy rows that have no county
cards.wall: PACER needs your own free PACER account and charges $0.10 a page, capped at $3.00 per document. Fees are waived if you stay under $30 a quarter (from 1 Jan 2027: $0.12 a page and a $40 waiver). CourtListener's RECAP archive is free and has many of the same documents.
cards.what: Bankruptcy rows come from the free CourtListener feed with the debtor's name and case number but often no address. Your coverage sheet counts about 5,000 such rows under 'UNKNOWN' county (about 3,060 in NC and 1,950 in SC); today's dashboard file shows 737. Page 1 of the bankruptcy petition lists the debtor's street address and county.
steps: First ask Claude to pull every petition that is already free in CourtListener's RECAP archive. That needs no person and no money, and may fix many rows at once.

saving_md: There is one ready-made lane, for court result lists:
1. Save the results page with **Cmd + S**, Format **Web Page, HTML Only**.
2. Name it `<county>_nc_<what>_<date>.html` for NC (the `_nc_` part is required; the loader reads the county from the text before it) or `<county>_sc_<what>_<date>.html` for SC.
3. Put it in the Desktop folder **Court Pages (drop here)**.

4. Double-click **Ingest Saved Court Pages** on the Desktop. It loads NC eCourts and SC Public Index lists, matches owner names to parcels, never makes duplicates, refuses to run while the weekly engine run is writing, and then moves the files into a dated 'Ingested' subfolder.

Watch out: that app moves **every** .html, .htm and .csv file out of the drop folder, whether or not it could read it. So save anything that is not a court list (contact sheets, probate pages, LiensNC pages, PDFs) into **~/Downloads** instead and tell Claude what you saved.

- **Lead checker** for one NC court case: Claude starts it, you pass the CAPTCHA and save the case page, Claude reads it.
- **LiensNC loader** for saved LiensNC result pages or CSV files.

Everything else (saved probate pages, notice pages, property-card sheets, county PDFs, bankruptcy address sheets, records-request replies) has **no loader yet**.
